planting.note: Soak seed overnight before direct sowing or starting indoors, since parsley germinates slowly and unevenly in cold soil; Darki is exceptionally winter hardy and can be left in the ground for a late-fall or overwintered harvest in milder zones.

directions: Darki is a French heirloom triple-curled parsley prized for its very dark green, densely ruffled leaves and heavy, repeat-cutting productivity through a long season. It holds up unusually well to cold, tolerating hard frosts and light freezes that flatten less hardy curly types, which makes it a favorite for late-fall harvest and overwintering in milder gardens. The compact, uniform plants stay attractive and upright rather than sprawling, so they work well massed as an edging or container planting. Cut outer leaves regularly to keep new growth coming and to delay the plant's second-year bolt into flower.

planting.note: Soak seed overnight to speed germination and direct sow or transplant after danger of hard frost; Katinka is a fast-establishing curled type bred for early, uniform stands.

directions: Katinka is a Dutch-bred curled parsley selected for very tightly ruffled, mid-green leaves on short, sturdy stems that resist flopping and stay clean off the soil surface. It germinates and establishes somewhat more reliably than older curly strains, giving a quicker, more even bed for market growers and home gardeners alike. The compact habit and dense curl make it a strong choice for garnish production and container growing on a patio or windowsill. Regular cutting of outer leaves keeps plants productive for months before they bolt.

planting.note: Soak seed overnight before sowing into cool, moist soil; Wega shows improved tolerance of leaf-spot pressure, which helps stands stay clean through humid summer weather.

directions: Wega is a European market-garden curled parsley bred with better field tolerance of Septoria leaf spot than many older curly strains, so foliage tends to stay cleaner and greener through the humid stretches of a long growing season. Leaves are tightly and evenly curled with a rich medium-green color that holds its quality well after cutting. Vigorous regrowth after each harvest makes it a dependable choice for gardeners who want several cuttings from one planting. It is grown the same way as other curly parsleys, with regular outer-leaf harvest to encourage continued production.

planting.note: Direct sow only, since cilantro resents root disturbance; Pokey Joe stays compact and leafy well after standard varieties have begun to bolt, so later spring sowings still produce a usable leaf harvest.

directions: Pokey Joe is a dwarf cilantro selected for a low, dense, mounding habit and a notably slow transition to flowering compared with standard cilantro. Its short stature keeps the fine-cut leaves close together and easy to shear for repeated cutting, and the compact size suits small beds, edging, and containers where taller cilantro would flop or crowd neighbors. Because it holds in leaf production longer before bolting, it extends the harvest window of a single spring sowing further into warm weather than older varieties typically allow. Succession sow every few weeks for a continuous supply, and let a few plants flower and set seed for coriander.

planting.note: Direct sow into cool, moist soil, since cilantro's taproot makes it a poor transplant candidate; Cruiser's slow-bolt habit gives more flexibility for later spring and early summer sowings than older open-pollinated types.

directions: Cruiser is a commercial hybrid cilantro bred for uniform, upright plants with broad, dark green leaves and a pronounced resistance to premature bolting under warm conditions. Its vigor and even stand make it a dependable choice for growers who need a predictable, heavy leaf harvest over a longer cutting window than standard varieties provide. The strong aromatic flavor is typical of full-size cilantro, making it suitable for fresh market bunching as well as home harvest. As with all cilantro, expect the plant to eventually flower and set coriander seed once day length and temperature rise, even on a slow-bolt selection like this one.

planting.note: Direct sow in cool soil a few weeks before last frost, or succession sow through early summer; Diplomat holds in the leafy stage notably longer than older dill varieties before flowering.

directions: Diplomat is a European-bred dill developed for commercial fresh-cut dill weed production, valued for tall, sturdy plants that resist lodging and a leafy stage that persists well before the plant switches to flowering. The blue-green foliage is finely cut and aromatic, holding good quality for bunching and fresh cutting over an extended harvest period. Its slower transition to bloom compared with older field varieties gives gardeners more flexibility in timing successive sowings through the cool part of the season. Allow a portion of the planting to flower and set seed heads if dill seed is also wanted for pickling.
sources: European commercial herb seed trade literature

planting.note: Direct sow into cool soil a few weeks before last frost, since dill's taproot resists transplanting; sow in succession every few weeks for continuous fresh dill weed.

directions: Goldkrone (German for 'golden crown') is a German dill selection bred for heavy foliage production and a strong, classic dill aroma, with feathery blue-green leaves borne on upright, well-branched plants. It is grown primarily for fresh and dried dill weed rather than seed, producing a full flush of cutting-quality foliage before bolting to flower. The variety performs reliably in the cool conditions dill favors and responds well to regular harvesting, which encourages continued leafy growth. As with other dill, plant it away from fennel to avoid cross-pollination if you intend to save seed.
